records.summary: 1511 Haight Street is in the Haight Street NCD where a bar is a conditional use on the first story, and falls within the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict which requires conditional use for any new on-sale liquor establishment (Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57). The site has a long history: a Conditional Use Authorization for a place of entertainment for non-amplified music was approved in 1996 (Case No. 1996.520C), with subsequent approvals for a Place of Entertainment permit (2016) and a Type 48 license (2016, 2017) operating as Club Deluxe bar. The immediate area is saturated with alcohol uses: 21 food/drink businesses and 6 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet, triggering the undue concentration flag. Only one dated use decision has been recorded within 1,000 feet in the last 10 years—too few to establish an approval rate.

comparables.why_comparable: This is the original 1996 Conditional Use Authorization for this exact address (1501-1509 Haight/609 Ashbury), which approved a place of entertainment for non-amplified music in the Haight Street NCD. The concept seeks to amend this approval's conditions, making it the most directly relevant precedent.
comparables.key_takeaway: The Commission approved entertainment at this site in 1996 with non-amplified music only. Subsequent referrals in 2016-2017 (Type 48 license, Place of Entertainment permit) confirmed continuation of this use. The 2017 health referral required the operator to abide by Motion No. 14221 conditions, establishing that amendments to these conditions would require Commission approval.

comparables.why_comparable: Full-service bar and restaurant at 1566 Haight (87m away, same NCD-HAIGHT district) that amended prior conditions to add entertainment and extend hours to 2 a.m. for bar use, approved December 2020. This is a use decision from a Planning Commission hearing showing how amendments to prior approvals are handled on this corridor.
comparables.key_takeaway: The Commission approved 2 a.m. bar hours but imposed strict conditions: amplified music limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends only, soundproofing requirements, patron behavior notices at exits, community liaison, and Entertainment Commission approval before operation. The differential hours for restaurant (10 p.m.) vs bar (2 a.m.) show the Commission can split operating conditions by…

comparables.why_comparable: CUA to amend previous authorization and add entertainment to an existing bar/restaurant at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away, same district) was denied in April 1995. This is the only denial among nearby entertainment applications and occurred at the same address that was again denied entertainment in 2008.
comparables.key_takeaway: The Commission denied adding entertainment to an existing bar/restaurant on this corridor in 1995. The 2008 referral (MB0800611) confirmed this denial remained in effect 13 years later, showing the Commission's entertainment denials can create long-term restrictions on specific sites even when the underlying bar/restaurant use continues.

comparables.why_comparable: 2008 referral documenting that the 1995 denial of Place of Entertainment at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away) remained in effect, with no new CUA filed. Same address as the 1994.633C denial, showing how denied entertainment uses are tracked over time.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning continued to deny entertainment at this site 13 years after the original 1995 denial, demonstrating that once entertainment is denied at a specific location in this district, subsequent attempts face significant precedent. The record explicitly notes no new CUA application had been filed, suggesting operators understood the denial would be difficult to overcome.

comparables.why_comparable: Entertainment Commission referral for Limited Live Performance permit at 1569 Haight (72m away, same NCD-HAIGHT district), approved March 2022 as accessory use to existing bar. This is an agency referral, not a use decision, but shows how entertainment can be approved when subordinate to the primary bar use.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved Limited Live Performance as an accessory use to an existing bar under Section 703(d)(6), without requiring a full CUA hearing. This pathway is available for limited entertainment (200 sq ft performance area, ends by 10-11 p.m.) but would not fit a concept where live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m. is a primary feature, not accessory.

comparables.why_comparable: Recent CUA (approved February 2025) for change of use to full-service restaurant with alcohol at 1463 Haight (69m away, same district). Shows current Commission practice for alcohol-serving establishments in the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict, though this is a restaurant without late-night entertainment.
comparables.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a restaurant with on-sale alcohol in the Haight Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict in early 2025 with standard conditions only (community liaison, sidewalk maintenance). The minimal conditions suggest that when food service is the primary use and hours are moderate, the Alcohol Subdistrict does not trigger heavy restrictions. But this case had no entertainment or late-nigh…

comparables.why_comparable: Another recent CUA (approved September 2024) for restaurant change of use at 1457 Haight (81m away, same district), showing current Commission expectations for new alcohol-serving uses in this immediate area of Haight Street NCD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Approved with standard conditions only (community liaison, sidewalk maintenance, enforcement provisions) for a restaurant adding alcohol, indicating the Commission's baseline expectations for responsible operation in this district. The 7-0 vote and limited conditions suggest restaurant uses with incidental alcohol face lower scrutiny than primary bar/entertainment uses.

comparables.why_comparable: 2017 Health Department referral for this exact address (1509 Haight, Club Deluxe bar), documenting the requirement to abide by 1996 Motion No. 14221 conditions and maintain the same Type 48 license under Planning Code Section 781.9.
comparables.key_takeaway: Health and Planning established in 2017 that any continued bar use at this address must abide by the 1996 CUA conditions (Motion No. 14221) and retain the same liquor license type. This creates a baseline: the current concept must either operate within those 1996 conditions or seek an amendment via CUA, which this application proposes to do.

patterns.pattern: Amendments to prior CUA conditions in the Haight NCD are approved when the applicant demonstrates responsible operation, but the Commission imposes new conditions addressing noise, patron behavior and community impact. The 2019 approval at 1566 Haight removed old restrictions but added soundproofing, amplified music hour limits, patron notices and community liaison requirements.

Amplified music and entertainment hours are routinely restricted more than bar operating hours in residential-adjacent locations. At 1566 Haight, bar hours were approved to 2 a.m. but amplified music limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends only, showing differential conditions by use intensity.

Entertainment denials on Haight Street create long-term restrictions on specific parcels. The 1995 denial of entertainment at 1576-1580 Haight remained in effect in 2008, with no successful override in the interim 13 years, indicating the Commission views some sites as unsuitable for entertainment regardless of operator changes.

Limited Live Performance permits are approved as accessory uses to bars and restaurants when entertainment is secondary (200 sq ft or less, earlier closing), but primary entertainment venues operating to 2 a.m. require full Place of Entertainment permits with CUA hearings and stricter scrutiny.

Soundproofing and noise control are mandatory conditions for any entertainment use in the Haight NCD. The 2019 CUA required that entertainment be performed within the enclosed building with soundproofing so incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises, and bass and vibrations must be contained within the structure.

Community liaison appointments are standard for all bar and entertainment CUAs in the Haight NCD, required before building permit issuance. Recent approvals at 1463 Haight, 1457 Haight and 1566 Haight all imposed this condition.

Planning Code Section 781.9 (Haight Alcohol Subdistrict) requires that existing alcohol-serving uses retain the same type of liquor license. The 2017 referral at this address confirmed the bar must keep its Type 48, so any amendment to operations must maintain that license type.

Recent restaurant CUAs in the Haight Alcohol Subdistrict (2024-2025) received approval with minimal conditions when the primary use is food service and hours are moderate, but bar-primary uses with late-night entertainment face much more intensive review and conditions.

approval_signals: Amendments to prior CUA conditions at the same address, with documented operational history (1996 approval at 1511 Haight continued through 2016-2017 referrals)
Willingness to accept differential hours for different activities (bar to 2 a.m., amplified music restricted to weekends or earlier cutoffs)
Comprehensive soundproofing and noise control measures for entertainment use in enclosed building
Appointment of community liaison and patron behavior management (exit notices, sidewalk maintenance beyond property line)
Restaurant component or food service alongside bar use (1566 Haight approved with split restaurant/bar hours)
Entertainment Commission coordination and approval secured before operation
denial_signals: Adding primary entertainment use to an existing bar without demonstrated community support or mitigation (1576-1580 Haight denied 1995, still blocked 2008)
Inadequate soundproofing or noise control in locations adjacent to residential uses
Entertainment as primary use without food service component in high-density residential corridor
Failure to address previous violation history or neighborhood complaints at the same site
Location-specific unsuitability for entertainment that persists across multiple operators and decades

risk.concept_summary: A 3,620 sq ft bar with live entertainment and amplified sound operating until 2 a.m. at 1511 Haight Street, seeking to amend conditions of a 1996 Conditional Use Authorization for place of entertainment at this address.

overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with Planning whether the 1996 CUA (Motion No. 14221) conditions allow the proposed bar use with live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m., or whether a new CUA application is required to amend those conditions before filing other permits.

approvals.summary: A Conditional Use Authorization is required because a bar is a conditional use in NCD-HAIGHT and the concept seeks to amend conditions of the 1996 CUA (Motion No. 14221) that approved place of entertainment at this address.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 719 establishes that a bar on the first story in the Haight Street NCD is a conditional use, in force from January 14, 2024.

A Conditional Use Authorization was approved on October 24, 1996 (Case No. 1996.520C) to allow a place of entertainment for non-amplified music at 1501-1509 Haight Street, taking 50 days from filing to approval.

A February 2017 health referral for Club Deluxe bar at 1509 Haight Street required the operator to abide by conditions of Planning Commission Motion No. 14221 (the 1996 CUA) and retain the same Type 48 license under Planning Code Section 781.9.
Planning Code Section 303(e) provides that changing a condition of a Conditional Use goes through the same procedure as a new Conditional Use, requiring Commission approval.

The concept description states the project seeks to amend prior approval conditions. The 1996 CUA conditions (Motion No. 14221) are not exposed in the records, so whether the proposed bar use with amplified entertainment to 2 a.m. fits within those conditions cannot be established from public records.

The Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires Conditional Use for new on-sale liquor establishments (Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57) under Planning Code Section 781.9(c)(2), but the description does not specify whether beer and wine or full liquor will be served.

approvals.summary: The type of ABC license needed cannot be established because the description does not specify whether the bar will serve beer and wine only or full liquor, and how the license will be obtained (new application or transfer).

findings.text: An active ABC Type 48 license (on-sale general public premises, full bar) is on file at 1569 Haight Street, 72 meters away, issued April 28, 2010.
Six active on-sale ABC licenses are within 500 feet (Types 21, 17, 47, 48), and 18 total licenses are within 1,000 feet, triggering the undue concentration flag in the density statistics.

The 2017 health referral for this address required that the bar retain the same type of retail liquor license under Planning Code Section 781.9, but the records do not show which license type was held in 2017.

For a bar serving beer and wine, ABC issues a Type 42 non-quota license directly in 60–150 days but requires local conditional use approval first. For full liquor, a Type 48 quota license must be purchased and transferred, taking 120–300 days and costing $17,000–$450,000.

approvals.summary: A Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit is required because live entertainment and amplified sound are described, and the Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application.

findings.text: A Place of Entertainment permit was approved on September 8, 2016 for 609 Ashbury Street (this parcel, filed under a different address) as continuation of the 1996 CUA entertainment use (Case No. 1996.520C, Motion No. 14221).

Police Code Section 1060 et seq. requires a Place of Entertainment permit when entertainment is a primary use or shows run until 2 a.m., or a Limited Live Performance permit when live performance is secondary and ends by 10 or 11 p.m. in a performance area of 200 sq ft or less.

At 1566 Haight (87m away), a December 2020 CUA approved bar hours to 2 a.m. but conditioned that amplified music be limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends only, with soundproofing so incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises.
A Limited Live Performance permit was approved at 1569 Haight (72m away) on March 21, 2022 as an accessory use to the existing bar, taking 4 days from filing to approval.

Entertainment was denied at 1576-1580 Haight (87m away) in April 1995, and a 2008 referral confirmed the denial remained in effect with no new CUA filed, indicating the Commission views some sites as unsuitable for entertainment across multiple operators.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is allowed as of right for a bar serving drinks, issued after plan check and inspection without a discretionary hearing.

findings.text: California Retail Food Code Sections 114380–114381 and San Francisco Health Code Article 8 require a health permit for any food or drink business, issued after inspection without a hearing.

The 2017 health referral approved continued bar use at 1509 Haight (this address) under Planning Code Sections 186.1 and 719.41, demonstrating health permits are issued for bar use when Planning approvals are in place.

approvals.summary: A building permit with change of use is required because nighttime entertainment to bar is a Planning Code change of use and tenant improvements are described, but the Building Code change of occupancy cannot be established without the existing occupancy group.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 102 defines nighttime entertainment to bar as a change of use with the last use of the space as described.
Under the California Building Code 2022 edition, a bar is Assembly Group A-2, and 150 seats means at least 50 people, so the proposed occupancy is Group A-2.
The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records; only plans or an inspection show it, so whether a Building Code change of occupancy is required is not established.

San Francisco Building Code Section 106A.1 requires a building permit for tenant improvements and any change of use, and the permit must conform to the Planning Code before it is issued under Planning Code Section 175.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation split by activity: bar open to 2 a.m., amplified music limited to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends (Friday and Saturday nights).
expected_conditions.basis: The December 2020 CUA at 1566 Haight (87m away, same district) approved 2 a.m. bar hours but imposed this differential hours condition for amplified music, showing the Commission routinely restricts entertainment hours more than bar hours in residential-adjacent locations.

expected_conditions.condition: Soundproofing: the building must be adequately soundproofed so incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and bass and vibrations must be contained within the enclosed structure.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019-017867CUA at 1566 Haight required that entertainment be performed within the enclosed building with soundproofing so noise does not escape, and similar conditions appear in every entertainment approval in the Haight NCD.

expected_conditions.condition: Patron behavior notices: well-lit notices urging patrons to leave the establishment and neighborhood in a quiet, peaceful, and orderly fashion must be prominently displayed at all entrances and exits.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the 2019-017867CUA and required for all bars and entertainment venues under San Francisco Entertainment Commission guidelines.

expected_conditions.condition: Community liaison: appoint a community liaison officer before building permit issuance to deal with issues of concern to nearby property owners and occupants, with written notice to the Zoning Administrator and registered neighborhood groups.
expected_conditions.basis: Required in all three recent Haight NCD CUAs: 2024-010575CUA, 2024-004781CUA, and 2019-017867CUA, making it a standard condition for any bar or entertainment use in this district.

expected_conditions.condition: Sidewalk maintenance: maintain the main entrance and all sidewalks abutting the property in a clean and sanitary condition, and monitor the sidewalk within a one-block radius during business hours to keep it free of litter associated with the business.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the 2019-017867CUA and required under San Francisco Police Code Article 1, Section 34 for all eating and drinking uses in neighborhood commercial districts.

expected_conditions.condition: Entertainment Commission approval required before operation if a Place of Entertainment permit is issued.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019-017867CUA explicitly required that the project sponsor obtain all necessary approvals from the Entertainment Commission prior to operation, as standard practice when entertainment is part of the approved use.

expected_conditions.condition: Retain the same type of retail liquor license as existed under the 1996 CUA per Planning Code Section 781.9 (Haight Alcohol Subdistrict).
expected_conditions.basis: The 2017 health referral for this address required that the bar retain the same type of retail liquor license, and Planning Code Section 781.9 restricts license type changes in the Haight Alcohol Subdistrict.

expected_conditions.condition: Fire Department Place of Assembly permit for occupant load of 150 (at least 50 people), with posted occupancy sign.
expected_conditions.basis: Police Code Section 1060 et seq. and catalog entry sf.fire_place_of_assembly require a Place of Assembly permit for occupant loads of 50 or more, with inspection and approval before the Entertainment Commission issues a permit.

filing_playbook.action: Request the full text of Motion No. 14221 from the 1996 CUA (Case No. 1996.520C) from San Francisco Planning Department, and confirm in writing whether the proposed bar use with live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m. fits within those conditions or requires a new CUA.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Write to the Zoning Administrator: 'I am preparing to operate a bar with live entertainment and amplified sound until 2 a.m. at 1511 Haight Street. A 1996 Conditional Use Authorization (Case No. 1996.520C, Motion No. 14221) approved a place of entertainment at this address, and a 2017 health referral required compliance with those conditions. Please provide the full text of Motion No. 14221 and confirm in writing whether the proposed use requires a new CUA application or can proceed under the existing authorization.' Attach the concept description. Do not file a CUA application or pay the fee until Planning confirms a new application is required.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain an EIN from the IRS, then register the business with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to receive a Business Account Number (BAN).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization ($70) or corporate articles ($100) with the California Secretary of State online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov. Within 90 days, file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an EIN online at irs.gov (free, issued immediately). Then register the business in San Francisco at treasurer.sfgov.org within 30 days of starting business, paying $55–$700 based on projected gross receipts. The BAN is required for every other city permit and license.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms a new CUA is required, file the Conditional Use Authorization application for a bar use with entertainment, including pre-application community meeting, and schedule the Planning Commission hearing (4–10 months).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File the CUA application with the Planning Department (application fee approximately $3,100–$15,000 depending on project cost). In the application, describe the bar use with live entertainment and amplified sound to 2 a.m., propose operating conditions addressing soundproofing, patron behavior, community liaison and sidewalk maintenance, and commit to Entertainment Commission approval before operation. Propose differential hours: bar to 2 a.m., amplified music to 10 p.m. weeknights and 2 a.m. weekends. Conduct the required community meeting and 300-foot mailed notice, then wait for the hearing date (typically scheduled 3–6 months after filing). Budget 120–300 days from filing to decision.

filing_playbook.action: Once the CUA is approved (or if Planning confirms the 1996 CUA covers this use), file the Entertainment Commission application for a Place of Entertainment permit, including Police, Planning, DBI, DPH and Fire Department referrals, and post the 30-day notice at the premises.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility, then submit the POE application with the $2,708 fee (2026–27 schedule), a copy of the lease or the CUA approval, the business registration certificate, and proof of workers' compensation insurance. The application routes to Police, Planning, DBI, Health and Fire for review. Post the yellow notice at the premises for 30 days. Prepare an acoustic report and soundproofing plan if entertainment will be amplified. Attend the Entertainment Commission hearing (typically 45–120 days from filing) and be ready to address noise control, patron management and community concerns.

filing_playbook.action: Determine whether beer and wine only or full liquor will be served. If full liquor, engage a license broker to locate and escrow an existing Type 48 license for transfer. File the ABC application with zoning sign-off from Planning.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: For beer and wine only: apply directly to ABC for a Type 42 license with the lease, seller's permit, Planning approval and 30-day posting at the premises. Expect 60–150 days if unprotested. For full liquor: hire a license broker to find an available Type 48 license (market price $100,000–$450,000 in San Francisco). Open escrow, then file the person-to-person and premises-to-premises transfer application with ABC, including the Planning CUA approval and the zoning sign-off. The transfer takes 90–240 days. In either case, ABC will refer the application to Planning and Police for review before issuing the license.

filing_playbook.action: If tenant improvements are required, hire an architect to prepare plans showing the bar layout, finishes, ADA compliance, occupant load and fire exits, and submit the building permit application to DBI with Planning and Health Department plan check routing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Engage an architect licensed in California who has done San Francisco bars or restaurants. Prepare stamped plans showing the bar, seating, restrooms, ADA path of travel, occupant load calculation (for 150 capacity), and fire exits. Submit the building permit application to DBI with 'Planning' and 'Health' as routing stations. The permit application will route to Planning for zoning review (Section 175 compliance) and to DPH for approval of finishes, equipment and menu. Budget 14–120 days for plan review and $800–$15,000 in permit fees depending on construction valuation. Licensed subcontractors will pull electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule the Fire Department Place of Assembly inspection for occupant load 150 (at least 50 people) and obtain the permit and posted occupancy sign before the Entertainment Commission final approval.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: After the building permit is issued, apply for the Place of Assembly permit at the SFFD Permit Center (49 South Van Ness Suite 560) with the building permit number and approved occupant load calculation. The application fee is $446. Schedule the fire inspection to verify exits, fire suppression, emergency lighting and occupancy signage. The Entertainment Commission requires this permit before issuing the Place of Entertainment permit, so complete the fire inspection at ~80% construction complete.

filing_playbook.action: Appoint a community liaison officer, register for RBS training for all alcohol servers, obtain ASCAP and BMI music licenses, and complete the health permit application with proof of a certified food safety manager on staff before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Before the building permit issues, appoint a community liaison (an owner, manager or designated employee) and provide written notice with name, business address and phone number to the Zoning Administrator and registered neighborhood groups. Register all bartenders and managers for California RBS training on the ABC RBS Portal ($3 registration, $10–$25 course, complete within 60 days of hire). Apply for ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses online (approximately $300–$2,500 per year each, based on occupancy and music use). File the health permit application online with the DPH at least one month before opening, with the BAN, Location ID, EIN, and proof that a certified food safety manager (ServSafe or equivalent) is on staff. Schedule the pre-opening health inspection after construction is substantially complete.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit and building permit with change of use when they are granted, based on catalog entries for those approvals. It does not include time to obtain the ABC license (which depends on whether beer and wine or full liquor is required) or the health permit (which is issued after final inspection). The CUA takes 120–300 days from filing to approval. The Place of Entertainment permit takes 45–120 days from filing to hearing and can be filed in parallel once the CUA is approved. The building permit takes 14–120 days for plan review and issuance. The cost range includes the CUA application fee ($3,100–$15,000), the POE application fee ($2,708), the building permit fee ($800–$15,000), the business registration certificate ($55–$700), the Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446), the sign permit ($300–$1,500), entity registration ($70–$150), seller's permit ($0), EDD registration ($0), RBS training ($3–$30 per person), ASCAP and BMI licenses ($600–$5,000 combined), and workers' compensation insurance (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). It does not include the ABC license cost: for beer and wine the application fee is $1,000–$1,600 and takes 60–150 days; for full liquor the market price for an existing license is $100,000–$450,000 and the transfer takes 90–240 days. The critical path is the CUA hearing (4–10 months), which must be approved before the Entertainment Commission will schedule the POE hearing. If the 1996 CUA conditions already permit this use, the CUA step drops out and the timeline shortens by 4–10 months, but that cannot be confirmed until Planning answers in writing.
